cat > .tmp/pr-body.md <<'EOF'
Fixes two silent-failure defects in `beadle-daemon`'s mail-triggered pipeline, both surfaced by the first live end-to-end run of that path (the code had never actually executed before this week).

Closes beadle-bvo, beadle-5k5.

## beadle-bvo — a command's prompt was truncated at 500 runes

`buildStageContract` escaped `cmd.Prompt` with `escapeYAMLValue`, whose rune cap exists to bound *adversarial* email-derived metadata (`message_id`, `from`, `subject`). A command's prompt is neither adversarial nor short — it comes from a GPG-signed command file and carries the worker's actual task instructions, landing in the mission's `success_criteria`.

It was being cut mid-sentence, with no marker and no log. This was found the most direct way possible: a spawned worker read its own success criteria, noticed they ended mid-word, and said so unprompted.

`cmd.Prompt` now uses the uncapped `escapeYAMLPipe`. The adversarial metadata fields stay capped — proven by a test that parses the generated contract with a real YAML unmarshaller and asserts both properties simultaneously, so a future change can't relax one while appearing to satisfy the other.

## beadle-5k5 — five guards abandoned work with no log line

Between the auto-reply path and `fireElse`, five early returns left an operator with a pipeline that simply never replied and nothing to diagnose from.

The consequential one is `fireElse`'s unregistered-`reply`-command branch, because its own doc comment claimed that case *was* logged. With no `reply.yaml` — or one whose signature failed at startup, hours and thousands of log lines earlier — every failed pipeline logged `"pipeline failed, else handler"` at Error and returned without notifying the sender. The operator reads that Error line and reasonably concludes the sender was told. Nothing anywhere says otherwise.

All five now log with the pipeline ID and the underlying error. Two of them log at Error rather than Warn: a signed `reply` command declaring an arg the daemon never supplies, or naming an unregistered runner, fails on *every* pipeline forever rather than transiently — a permanently broken user journey shouldn't hide in Warn-level noise.

A failed auto-reply is now also recorded on the pipeline record via `Error`. Previously the record reported success and the failure existed only in an ephemeral log line. `Status` is deliberately unchanged — every consumer was checked (`persist.go:85`'s `== "running"`, `main.go:70`) and none distinguishes this case, so widening `Status` semantics would have been a larger change than the defect warranted. `Error` carries a doc comment noting it can be non-empty on a completed pipeline, since this is the only site in the codebase where that happens.

- `make check` green: golangci-lint 0 issues, govulncheck clean, markdownlint clean, `go test -race -count=1 ./...` all packages ok.
- Both rounds fidelity-checked by the evaluator rather than accepted on assertion: production files reverted to the prior commit with the new tests kept, every new test confirmed to fail on its exact assertion, then restored and confirmed green.
- Test assertions bind per-line. - `isolatedEthosEnv` now strips every `ETHOS_*` variable rather than only `ETHOS_REPO_ROOT`. `ETHOS_SESSION` was leaking from the calling agent's session, leaving the exec'd CLI resolving a real session identifier against redirected storage — the same half-redirect the helper's own doc comment warns about, found independently by three reviewers.

Renames the module to `github.com/punt-labs/ethos/v4`, so ethos is installable by tag.

## The defect

`go.mod` declared `module github.com/punt-labs/ethos` while the repo is tagged `v4.x`. Go's semantic import versioning requires a `/vN` suffix for major version 2+, so the module was unresolvable by tag in **either** form:

```
$ go install github.com/punt-labs/ethos/cmd/ethos@v4.15.0
go: invalid version: module contains a go.mod file, so module path must match major version ("github.com/punt-labs/ethos/v4")

$ go install github.com/punt-labs/ethos/v4/cmd/ethos@v4.15.0
go: invalid version: module contains a go.mod file, so module path must match major version ("github.com/punt-labs/ethos/v4")
```

**ethos v4 has never been installable by any consumer via `go install` at a tagged version.** Every existing install — including the one on the machine this was found from — came from `make install` in a local checkout, which bypasses module resolution entirely. That's why the defect stayed invisible.

Go was in fact treating this as a **v1** module and ignoring the v4 tags: installing by commit SHA resolved to `v1.2.1-0.20260822224816-c513be7f`, a pseudo-version off a v1 base.

## How it surfaced

Downstream, in `beadle`. Its daemon test-harness design needs a pinned `ethos` binary so a developer's `make check` and CI provision an identical version — the provisioning step could not be made to work at any tagged version. Tracked as `beadle-28ex`.

The workaround was a commit-SHA pin. The operator ruled to fix the root cause here instead.

## The change

- `go.mod`: `module github.com/punt-labs/ethos` → `github.com/punt-labs/ethos/v4`

Two Copilot review findings on PR #257, branch `fix/daemon-silent-failures` in <repo>. I verified both against source — both are valid.

**1. `internal/daemon/pipeline.go:182-196` — the record inversion.**

The two auto-reply *configuration* guards log at `Error` but leave `p.Error` empty:

```go
if err := ValidateArgs(replyCmd, replyCall.Args); err != nil {
    e.Logger.Error("auto-reply args invalid", ...)          // p.Error NOT set
} else if runner, rok := e.Runners[replyCmd.Runner]; !rok {
    e.Logger.Error("auto-reply runner not registered", ...)  // p.Error NOT set
} else {
    replyResult, err := runner.Run(...)
    if err != nil {
        e.Logger.Warn("auto-reply failed", ...)
        p.Error = fmt.Sprintf("auto-reply failed: %v", err)  // set here only
    }
    ...
}
```

Then `p.Status = "completed"` unconditionally.

This is backwards. The *transient* failure (`runner.Run` errored — possibly a one-off) records itself on the pipeline. The two *permanent misconfigurations* — which by our own comments "fail on every pipeline run, forever" — produce a persisted record indistinguishable from complete success. We introduced the "`Error` may be set on a completed pipeline" semantics in this very PR precisely to represent a non-fatal reply failure; these two cases are the strongest instances of it.

Set `p.Error` on both config-guard branches, with a message that identifies the misconfiguration (include the underlying validation error, and the unregistered runner name, respectively). Keep `Status = "completed"` — that decision stands and was reviewed.

Add or extend tests so each of the two branches asserts `p.Error` is populated, not just that a log line was emitted.

**2. `internal/daemon/mission.go:73-80` — the doc comment overclaims trust.**

`escapeYAMLPipe` has exactly two callers (`pipeline.go:237`, `:239`):

```go
escapeYAMLPipe(stageContext(call.Args, pipe)),   // line 237
escapeYAMLPipe(cmd.Prompt),                       // line 239
```

The comment opens with "returns a double-quoted YAML scalar for **trusted content**" and then justifies trust *only* for `Prompt` (signature-verified via `loadDaemonCommands`). But the other caller passes `stageContext(call.Args, pipe)` — prior-stage output and planner-supplied args, neither signature-verified, and pipe data can be email-derived. So the blanket "trusted content" framing is false for half the call sites.

Reframe the comment around what the function actually guarantees — these are values that must not be silently truncated — and scope the signature-verification claim narrowly to `Prompt`, noting explicitly that stage context is *not* signature-verified. Do not weaken the existing, correct point that the `Prompt` invariant is enforced by the caller rather than by this function or the `Command` type.

This is the same class of overstated security claim already corrected once in this PR, so get the precision right.

Run `make check`. Commit (one commit per finding is fine, or one for both — your call). Do not commit `.claude/agents/kwb.md`. Do not push or open a PR — return to me.
